Evidence record
When was it measured or observed?2024–2026
Who or what does it apply to?Payment-reform rules, projects, decisions and institutions documented by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), the World Bank and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with rules, projects, integration, institutions, operation and use kept separate

How the payment architecture is changing

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

The recorded payment-reform steps from June 2024 to August 2026 sit at separate stages. Rules: Governor's Decision No. 23 of 2024, issued by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), requiring exchange companies, exchange establishments and money-transfer agents to execute new domestic cash transfers only through the unified money-transfer network (26 June 2024). Project: the World Bank-financed Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (FMIIP), approved by the World Bank's Board on 17 June 2025 and effective from 1 September 2025, with components supporting the development of a Fast Payment System (FPS) and the establishment of a Real-Time Gross Settlement system (RTGS). Decisions and institutions: a CBY-Aden board decision on what it calls a mandatory national QR standard (29 March 2026), unified-network integration work (17 June 2026), restructuring of the Unified Money Network company (27 July 2026) and the founding assembly of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC) on 3 August 2026. The FMIIP baseline for January 2025 records FPS and RTGS as not yet operational, with no participating institutions, and the status the project last reported, measured the day before it became effective, records neither as operational. The only information on use is a January 2026 CBY-Aden statement about activity on the unified network, which is CBY-Aden's own statement, not an independent measurement.

Another view of the evidence
01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

Dated payment-reform steps — rules, project components, decisions, integration work and new institutions — recorded between June 2024 and August 2026, each at the furthest stage its evidence supports.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Payment-reform rules, projects, decisions and institutions documented by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), the World Bank and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with rules, projects, integration, institutions, operation and use kept separate

04How current is it?

The latest step in this record is the founding of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC), whose founding assembly met on 3 August 2026 and whose board first met on 4 August 2026. The record should not be read as describing a later stage unless newer official evidence is published.

05What this evidence does not establish

A rule, project component, integration decision or new institution is not evidence of operation, adoption, transaction activity or a financial-inclusion outcome. The Fast Payment System (FPS) and the Real-Time Gross Settlement system (RTGS) are not shown to be operating: the baseline of the Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (FMIIP) for January 2025 records both as not yet operational. The World Bank's implementation report of 8 April 2026 reports both as not operational at 31 August 2025, the day before the project became effective, and, by its own date, the RTGS tender launched and the FPS tender expected to be published shortly; no later operational state is recorded.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Each step is taken from its official source — decisions and news records of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), the World Bank project record and implementation report, and the UNDP project page — and placed at the furthest stage its evidence supports: rule, project component, integration, institution, operation or observed use.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
